title: Redirect stdout and stderr
summary: dup2 inside the program: the equivalent of `> FILE 2>&1`, and the buffering trap that comes with it.
hints: Order matters: print the first line and `fflush(stdout)` **before** `dup2`, otherwise the buffered text is written later, into the file.

Make the redirection with one `open(FILE, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644)` and two `dup2` calls (onto 1 and onto 2), then `close` the extra descriptor. After redirecting, `fflush(stdout)` after each `printf` keeps the lines in the order you printed them (`stderr` is not buffered).
